unit.title: Getting Someone Else to Do It

grammar_concept.title: Causative: Have/Get Something Done
grammar_concept.rule: Use 'have/get + object + past participle' to say that someone else does something for you — you arrange it or pay for it, but you don't do the action yourself.
grammar_concept.simple_explanation: This structure exists specifically to mark that YOU didn't personally do the action — a professional or someone else did it, usually because you asked or paid them to. 'Get' is more informal than 'have', but both work the same way.
grammar_concept.example: I had my hair cut yesterday. She's getting her car repaired this week.
grammar_concept.example_translation: Cortei o cabelo ontem (no cabeleireiro). Ela vai arranjar o carro esta semana (na oficina).
grammar_concept.common_mistake_pt: Em português, usa-se o mesmo verbo na voz ativa mesmo quando foi outra pessoa que fez o trabalho ("cortei o cabelo", "vou arranjar o carro"), sem marcar gramaticalmente se foi a própria pessoa ou um profissional contratado. Isso leva a dizer "I cut my hair" quando na verdade se quer dizer que foi ao cabeleireiro — em inglês, "I cut my hair" significa especificamente que a PRÓPRIA pessoa pegou numa tesoura e cortou, sozinha, o que muda completamente o sentido.
grammar_concept.correction: Sempre que um profissional ou outra pessoa faz algo por si (cortar o cabelo, arranjar o carro, pintar a casa), use "have/get + objeto + particípio passado" ("I had my hair cut", "I got the car fixed") — nunca o verbo simples na ativa, que implica ter feito o trabalho pessoalmente.
grammar_concept.real_world_example: Talking about home repairs: "We're getting the roof fixed next month."

vocabulary.translation_pt: mandar fazer / ter algo feito (por outra pessoa)
vocabulary.definition_en: to arrange for someone else to do something for you
example_sentences: I need to have my car serviced soon.

vocabulary.definition_en: a person whose job is to cut and style hair
example_sentences: I have an appointment at the hairdresser's tomorrow.

vocabulary.definition_en: to fix something that is broken or damaged
example_sentences: The mechanic repaired the engine in one day.

exercises.prompt: Complete: I ___ (have) my hair cut yesterday.
exercises.explanation: "Had my hair cut" = alguém cortou o cabelo por mim, no passado — "had" é a forma correta de "have" no Past Simple aqui.
exercises.common_mistake_pt: Usar "I cut my hair" para dizer que foi ao cabeleireiro é o erro mais comum — essa frase significa que a pessoa cortou o cabelo sozinha.

exercises.prompt: Complete: We ___ (get) the roof fixed next month.
exercises.explanation: Plano combinado para o futuro próximo — Present Continuous com valor de futuro: "are getting".
exercises.common_mistake_pt: "Will got" não existe em inglês ("will" nunca é seguido de um verbo no passado) — erro comum ao tentar formar o futuro.

correct_answer: to arrange for someone else to do something for you
distractors: to plan to do something in the future
exercises.explanation: A estrutura marca especificamente que outra pessoa faz a ação, não o próprio falante.

exercises.prompt: Listen to the audio. What is the speaker having done to their car?
exercises.explanation: No áudio, ouve-se: "I'm having my car repaired at the garage down the street."
exercises.transcript: I'm having my car repaired at the garage down the street — it should be ready by Friday, so I've booked a rental car for the rest of the week.

exercises.prompt: Read: "Marta had her kitchen redecorated last month. She didn't do any of the work herself — she hired a local company to do it." Who actually did the decorating work?
exercises.explanation: O texto diz diretamente que ela "hired a local company to do it" — não fez o trabalho pessoalmente.

exercises.prompt: Translate to English: "Vou cortar o cabelo amanhã, no cabeleireiro."
correct_answer: I'm having my hair cut tomorrow.
I'm getting my hair cut tomorrow.
exercises.explanation: Como é o cabeleireiro que corta, não a própria pessoa, usa-se a estrutura causativa "having/getting my hair cut", nunca "I'm cutting my hair".
exercises.common_mistake_pt: Traduzir para "I'm cutting my hair tomorrow" é o erro mais comum — essa frase significaria que a pessoa vai cortar o próprio cabelo sozinha.

lesson.title: Getting Someone Else to Do It

steps.content: In fast speech, "have" in this structure is very weak — "I have my car fixed" often sounds like /aɪv mi kɑːr fɪkst/, almost merging into the pronoun, unlike when "have" is the main verb meaning "to possess".

steps.prompt: Talk about something you have had done recently (a haircut, a repair, a service) — who did it, and why you didn't do it yourself.
Write 3 sentences about things you have had done, are having done, or plan to have done, using "have/get + object + past participle".
